title: SO(4,1) Euclidean Conformal Group on (3,0) Eckert Manifold
premise: α is spacelike. Signature is (3,0). SO(4,2) does not apply.

key_findings: The Eckert manifold is ISOMETRICALLY FLAT (not just conformally flat). The Fisher product metric on (0,1)³ is a product of 1D flat spaces. Angular coordinates make this manifest: ds² = 4(dφ_O² + dφ_R² + dφ_α²).
SO(4,1) algebra closes exactly on the Eckert manifold (max error 0.00e+00). The conformal group IS SO(4,1).
Casimir C₂ = -2.0000 (nontrivial). The SO(4,1) representation has invariant content.
ED lift gives de Sitter signature (4,1). The natural "spacetime" of the Eckert manifold is de Sitter, not Minkowski. Poincaré symmetry appears via Inönü-Wigner contraction (Λ→0 limit).

Pe breaks ALL continuous SO(4,1) generators. The conformal symmetry of the base is completely broken by the dynamics. Pe preserves only discrete S₃ (permutation of O, R, α). The Pe function is NOT a Casimir — it is a specific function on the representation space.

Cross-domain universality (20 convergences, |ρ|=0.958) does NOT require any conformal group. It follows from FP universality on a Bernoulli manifold (Option A). Both SO(4,1) and SO(4,2) are explanatory surplus for the current empirical results.
verdict: The (3,0) Eckert manifold has conformal group SO(4,1) (de Sitter group, 10 generators). The algebra closes, the Casimir is nontrivial, and the ED lift gives de Sitter signature (4,1). Pe breaks all continuous conformal generators — the dynamics is NOT conformally invariant. Cross-domain universality is explained by FP universality, not group theory. SO(4,2) adds structure (Minkowski, hydrogen, 6 tradition mappings) but requires the unproven α-timelike hypothesis. SO(4,1) is the mathematically honest symmetry group of the actual manifold.
